full_failure.cause: Test-side, source-level. hostEvents filters harness.hostEventsText, a disk read of environment.eventsFile (AppStateHarnessTests.swift:130-132). The host writes that file through RuntimeEventFileWriter, a BoundedRecordWriter on its own utility queue (RuntimeHost.swift:424-433), after the in-memory append. The test's settle observed the framed snapshot's bindings, a different path. Nothing in the test waited for the writer, so under full-suite load the file was read before the record was written. Production restarted the listener and emitted the event. Not a relay-1c regression: this path has no transparent proxy and no relay commands.
full_failure.why_not_polling: Polling the file for the asserted event (as :900 did) or sleeping (:902, :724) only widens the window. The negative file checks in the same file could pass vacuously. AppState deliberately keeps no host reference (AppState.swift:264), so a direct drain would cross the app/host boundary; no host reference or test hook was added.

correction.causal_boundary: The app's own Quit (beginQuit/finishQuit). admitQuit runs await flushEvents(), which awaits the events writer's drain through DiagnosticFlush.run, and only then flush?.quitDidEnd() (RuntimeHostLifecycle.swift:1017-1018). RuntimeQuitFlush.settled() is true only through quitDidEnd before the deadline (RuntimeQuitFlush.swift:85-99), and the quit operation reports completed(.quit) only when settled() is true (RuntimeHostControlOwner.swift:287). An event recorded before the Quit was admitted has therefore left the writer's queue when finishQuit() returns .settled(.completed).
correction.honest_scope: A completed Quit is logical quiescence, not proof that every diagnostic writer confirmed its records: DiagnosticFlush caps each wait at 2 s, and a drained queue includes records the writer failed. The post-drain file assertions still catch an actual loss, a failed write or an unconfirmed drain, since the file is then short.
correction.helper: One private helper, quitJoiningHostDiagnostics(_:file:line:) -> Bool, beside hostEvents in AppStateActivationParityTests.swift. It asserts beginQuit() is the first quit and that finishQuit()?.quit is .settled(.completed). Its doc states the scope above. hostEvents' doc now says it is a disk read and names the helper. The harness teardown's own quit joins (beginQuit returns false).
correction.rule: Runtime, listener, machine, ledger and saved-config assertions stay before the Quit, because the Quit tears the modules down. Exact event counts and negative event checks go after it. No event poll, no sleep, no weakened assertion, no host reference.
